extracted.intended_audience: museum administrators, MFA applicants, and IMLS program staff
extracted.subtask_short: MFA grant program evaluation and guidance
extracted.subtask_description: Criteria and guidance for designing, applying to, implementing, and evaluating Museums for America (MFA) grants, and for IMLS program improvement. Focuses on project design, community engagement, collections stewardship, evaluation practice, sustainability, and application process factors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Strengthening partnerships
rubrics_metrics.description: The majority of grantees that worked with partners indicated that the grant experience had strengthened existing partnerships or helped them to develop their partnership skills.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Grants should enable collaborative work; partnership outcomes include strengthened existing partnerships and improved partnership skills. Emphasize partner roles and sustainment plans in proposals and track partnership development as an outcome.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public image and visibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Eighty percent of grantees reported that their museums’ public image was strengthened by the MFA grant; a somewhat smaller number indicated increased visibility as a center of community learning.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposals and evaluations should measure changes in public image and visibility (e.g., awareness, use, perception as community learning center). Note that prestige of the IMLS award, programming, and partnerships can drive these outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Community relevance and engagement
rubrics_metrics.description: Interviewees were consistently enthusiastic about how the MFA project helped to strengthen the museum’s relevance to its community, citing enhanced community awareness and use and opportunities for greater engagement and long-term interactions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate depth and duration of community engagement, not just participation counts. Look for evidence that deeper engagement leads to deeper understanding of community needs (positive feedback loop).

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of evaluation and outcomes-based planning
rubrics_metrics.description: Grantees reported new capacities in using evaluation to learn how audiences received projects; many reported greater staff capacity in outcomes-based planning and evaluation. IMLS-produced materials on logic models, outcomes-based planning and evaluation were helpful.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Encourage logic-model-driven design and iterative formative/process evaluation. Provide templates and training; assess whether projects used evaluation findings to adapt implementation and whether staff gained evaluation skills.

rubrics_metrics.name: Summative evaluation and survey tools
rubrics_metrics.description: Grantees described increasing sophistication in summative evaluation knowledge and growing skill in using online survey tools and tailoring questionnaires to particular museum experiences.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Support development of appropriate instruments and online tools; evaluate quality of summative evaluation methods and whether instruments were tailored to experiences being measured.

rubrics_metrics.name: Collections stewardship and audience access
rubrics_metrics.description: The MFA program enabled development, sustainment, and expansion of stewardship of cultural heritage, particularly related to audience access to collections (e.g., unifying collections across sites, making content available digitally, inventories, new collections management plans, archival research, oral histories).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Measure both preservation activities (inventories, care) and access outcomes (public use, digital availability). Track types of stewardship activities and their link to audience access.

rubrics_metrics.name: Digitization and creation of new digital content
rubrics_metrics.description: Thirty-four percent of surveyed museums undertook digitization or collections activities; of museums that digitized, nearly a quarter digitized at least half of their collections and more than 80% created new digital content.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Capture scope of digitization (portion of collections) and whether new digital content was created. Evaluate how digitization increased access and whether it contributed to preservation and new interpretive possibilities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Expanding collections through research and oral histories
rubrics_metrics.description: Some museums contributed to stewardship by conducting oral histories and research that created new collections materials and documented existing collections; research sometimes led to new exhibiting approaches.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recognize and reward research/fieldwork outputs (oral histories, documentation) that expand or reinterpret collections. Include dissemination and curation plans for new materials.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sustainability of programs after grant period
rubrics_metrics.description: Nearly all respondents reported being at least somewhat successful in continuing MFA programming; three out of five characterized efforts as 'very successful.' Many projects were written into operating budgets or financed through additional grants or partners. But 'success' is not synonymous with 'sustainable.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess sustainability in multiple dimensions: continued activity, institutionalization (e.g., budgeted), and whether lessons/learning were embedded even if specific activities end. Track funding follow-on, budget integration, partner support, and relevance changes due to external factors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Value of experimentation and learning (projects with limited life-spans)
rubrics_metrics.description: Some grants were designed as periods of experimentation; principals expected some efforts to fade. Projects that met objectives, provided lessons, and raised questions were valuable even if not continued as-is.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Judge projects by learning generated and contributions to institutional knowledge and strategy, not solely by whether original activities continued. Include documentation of lessons learned and plans for institutional uptake.

rubrics_metrics.name: Institutional learning and ripple effects
rubrics_metrics.description: In the strongest cases, MFA grants extended beyond intended projects and had ripple effects throughout the museum (e.g., success prompted re-thinking of other programming or became an institutional theme).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate cross-institutional diffusion of project ideas (infusion into broader operations, themes across departments, retail/cafés). Collect evidence of policy/practice changes that originated from project work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Capacity building: organizational development and training
rubrics_metrics.description: Almost all (98%) respondents reported positive effects from MFA funding on institutional capacity. Although only 6% identified organizational development as a primary resource allocation focus, 60% conducted organizational development activities; the most common was training of staff, docents or volunteers (65%).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Track organizational development activities (training, research, evaluation, management plans) and correlate with capacity outcomes (staff cohesion, mission alignment). Support training as a core allowable/encouraged activity and document its effects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Internal and external collaboration skills
rubrics_metrics.description: Survey data suggest MFA grants enhanced skills to form collaborations both internally and with other organizations; more than half reported increased skills forming external partnerships and working across departments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include measures of collaboration capability (new partnerships, cross-departmental projects) and consider supporting cross-institutional networks as part of program design.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clarity of goals and formative evaluation integration
rubrics_metrics.description: The clarity of MFA goals, ability to continuously integrate findings of formative (process) evaluation into project design, and the prestige of the national award helped grantees overcome implementation challenges.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess whether proposals present clear goals and plans for using formative evaluation to adapt implementation. Emphasize connection to strategic plans and how evaluation informs mid-course corrections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Attracting additional funding and governance engagement
rubrics_metrics.description: Most surveyed museums reported MFA grant helped attract additional funding; successful completion may give other funders confidence. Just under one-fifth reported greater board involvement as a result of an MFA project.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Track follow-on funding and governance (board) engagement as outcomes. Encourage applicants to include plans for leveraging MFA success to secure additional support and board buy-in.

rubrics_metrics.name: Achievement of strategic goals and mission alignment
rubrics_metrics.description: Four-fifths reported success in meeting key benchmarks for strategic goals, and nearly half reported greater staff commitment to mission. Projects often fit closely with institutional mission and sometimes advanced or re-defined mission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Require applicants to articulate connections to institutional mission and measurable strategic benchmarks. Evaluate success relative to those benchmarks and note contributions to mission evolution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application process as capacity-building activity
rubrics_metrics.description: The MFA application process itself appears to have a positive impact on all applicants; 80% said the application process helped them apply for other funding, 78% increased awareness of their own resources/strengths, and 76% integrated outcomes-based planning.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider the application process part of field-building. Provide accessible guidance and sample applications; measure application-development impacts on applicants' internal capacities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Awareness and helpfulness of IMLS resources
rubrics_metrics.description: IMLS provides information sessions, sample applications, schedules, contact info, outcome-based planning materials, online course, audio conference calls, and webinars. At least 70% were aware of outreach and website resources; among those aware, over 95% reported resources as somewhat or very helpful.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain and publicize a suite of resources (sample applications, counseling, webinars, online courses). Track both awareness and perceived helpfulness, and tailor outreach to museum size and region.

rubrics_metrics.name: Equity of outreach and access (small museums)
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondents from small museums were significantly less likely to be aware of outreach and resources and were more likely to find grants.gov and application navigation difficult. Small museums often lack staff and funds to hire consultants.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design targeted outreach and assistance (navigation help, technical support, possibly allow or subsidize consultant costs) for small museums. Monitor differential awareness/use by museum size and region.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cost-sharing requirement (1:1 match) impacts
rubrics_metrics.description: The MFA grant requires a 1:1 cost-sharing component. More than half of respondents said cost-sharing influenced staffing costs (59%) and scope of work (55%); other impacts included non-labor costs (45%), project duration (36%), time to raise funds (31%), and type of MFA grant (24%).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Expect cost-share to shape project scale and staffing. Evaluate applicants’ realistic cost-sharing plans and consider guidance/tools to help small museums secure or document matches; track how cost-sharing affects feasibility and equity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Barriers to applying (staff, technical, cost-sharing)
rubrics_metrics.description: Lack of staff resources and the cost-sharing requirement can be barriers. The grants.gov process is daunting for small organizations; many hire consultants but cannot always afford them. Large museums increasingly use dedicated grant writers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify and mitigate common barriers: simplify online submission guidance, offer technical assistance, explore policies on allowing consultant fees in budgets, and provide templates/sample language to reduce applicant burden.

rubrics_metrics.name: Perceptions of application process quality (clarity, accessibility, review, feedback)
rubrics_metrics.description: Over 85% favorably rated accessibility of information, clarity of requirements, the review process, and feedback. Respondents from funded museums were more likely to strongly agree with positive statements. Differences exist by museum size and region.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain transparent review and feedback processes; monitor perception differences across subgroups. Improve clarity of budget instructions, evaluation requirements, and online submission as needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Likelihood to reapply and value of repeat applicants
rubrics_metrics.description: 82% indicated they are very likely to apply again; funded museums and repeat applicants are more likely to reapply. Funding rate for reapplications is strong, so encouraging reapplication is recommended.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Encourage resubmission and provide supports for redesigning unfunded applications. Track outcomes of resubmissions and promote success stories and mentorship between experienced grantees and new applicants.

rubrics_metrics.name: Status and outcomes of unfunded applications (resubmission, alternative funding, implementation)
rubrics_metrics.description: Few unfunded applications were redesigned resubmissions (14%). Over a third sought non-IMLS funding (67% of those seeking other funding received it). Over half (57%) implemented the unfunded project or a version of it; execution was more likely among those with application experience or prior funding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Collect and share information about paths for unfunded projects (plan B, other funders, scaled implementations). Support applicants in adapting proposals for other funders and in documenting partial implementations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Program-level recommendation: expand access through outreach and delivery mechanisms
rubrics_metrics.description: IMLS might explore which outreach activities and delivery mechanisms are most effective in reaching potential applicants; nearly 70% of surveyed applicants were aware of IMLS outreach activities, and 47% received information from associations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess outreach channels by region and museum size; increase targeted outreach in under-aware regions (e.g., Southeast, Mid-Atlantic) and for small museums; partner with national/regional/state associations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Program-level recommendation: assist with online application navigation
rubrics_metrics.description: IMLS might consider offering greater assistance in navigating the online application system especially for small museums with less technical capacity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide step-by-step guidance, dedicated helpdesk support, webinars, and potentially in-person workshops focused on Grants.gov and online submission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Program-level recommendation: share best practices and create peer networks
rubrics_metrics.description: IMLS could connect potential applicants to grantees experienced in project planning and create online platforms where cohorts of grantees share resources on project management, budgeting, outreach, evaluation, and planning.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Facilitate mentorship, cohort learning, and resource-sharing platforms; prioritize first-time and resubmitting applicants; structure cohorts by project stage or thematic area.

rubrics_metrics.name: Program-level recommendation: support evaluation practice (templates, intermediaries, shared evaluators)
rubrics_metrics.description: IMLS has an opportunity to develop templates museums could use to articulate indicators and impacts, facilitate field-wide conversations about measuring cumulative impact, provide models for working with outside evaluators, and possibly support evaluation intermediaries or shared evaluators for themed project subsets.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide implementation logs, indicator templates, guidance for interim measures toward long-term social change, models for contracting evaluators, and options for pooled evaluation services for clusters of similar projects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Program-level recommendation: measure community-wide and long-term impacts
rubrics_metrics.description: IMLS might consider strategies and indicators related to meeting broad, socially transformative goals that encompass a longer time horizon than current evaluations; interim evaluation measures co-created by museums and stakeholders could help articulate stages of social change (e.g., growth of social connections, social network maps).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Develop intermediate indicators and co-created metrics for long-term social outcomes; support longitudinal or multi-institution assessments and tools for mapping social networks and community impacts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Program-level recommendation: encourage cross-institutional assessment
rubrics_metrics.description: IMLS might look to expand thinking about assessing community-wide impacts in conjunction with activities conducted by other public institutions such as libraries to encourage greater collaboration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Promote joint evaluation frameworks, shared indicators, and collaborative projects across museums, libraries, and other public institutions to capture broader community impacts.
